This Toyota Sienna-Based Micro Camper Van Offers More Creature Comforts Than You Expect
30 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Small Vans Big World
Just HOW small is too small when it comes to camper vans? Well, it depends on who you ask. If you feel a small van can't be livable in any way, the project I'd like to share with you today might just change your mind.
Today's featured build is based on a 2023 Toyota Sienna minivan. It was created by Small Vans Big World, a Valparaiso, Indiana-based company specializing in custom tiny homes on wheels based on small vans like the Ford Transit Connect .
At first glance, most people will think this is a standard car. The only mods that subtly hint at the fact that it's a camper are on the roof – you'll notice an awning and a low-profile Yakima roof box with a flexible solar panel on top.
This rig comes with custom-made Small Vans Big World deflectors for all windows. Each deflector slots in between the slightly open window and the window frame.
Enter and you'll be greeted by an efficiently designed interior. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. Even though there's no wall, you can't easily pass from one area to the other because of the way the furniture is arranged. That said, you could make your way over in an emergency if needed.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Small Vans Big World Regarding aesthetics, the camper interior fits with the van's standard design perfectly. The stock vehicle has a two-tone finish, with a black ceiling upholstery and beige walls. Small Vans Big World added a beautiful slatted cedar ceiling with a vent fan and recessed LED light strips, light blue cabinetry, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring.
The living space is split into two key parts: an L-shaped kitchen in the front, behind the driver and passenger seats, and a seating/sleeping area toward the back.
The kitchen is instantly reachable once you step inside the van. Besides limiting access between the living space and the driver's cabin, the kitchen also blocks access from the passenger-side door. The Toyota Sienna has two sliding doors, one on each side.
The kitchen features a deep round stainless steel sink with a pull-out tap, a portable stove, and a swiveling table extension that you can adjust to fit however you're sitting. The sink's tap can be pulled out so much that you can use it outside as a sprayer. Moreover, there are some metal pieces fixed to the countertop that you can use to attach a microwave oven or a cutting board.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Small Vans Big World Several controls are integrated into the kitchen counter – you get a switch for the water pump, a light switch, and a battery monitor.
Regarding storage, the kitchen offers four open compartments. One of the open compartments holds the rig's "electrical heart," a Jackery Explorer 1000 portable power station . It has a 1,070 Wh capacity and a 1,500 W output.
The "hallway" space between the van's two key areas is quite limited, but enough for two people to rest their legs on the floor comfortably.
The rear part of the living space is taken up by what looks at first like a large bench. At the flip of a switch, you can activate the bench's fully automated system that folds the bench flat into a bed. Next to the bed switch, there are two dimmer switches for the ceiling's recessed lights. In this part of the van, you'll also find two soft-close drawers attached to heavy-duty slides and two reading lights.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Small Vans Big World If you exit the van and open the trunk, you'll gain access to the large garage underneath the bench. You just have to undo two bed platform latches and hook it to the trunk door to have enough space to load and unload things in the garage. It holds a water jug and, when fully empty, it can accommodate at least two carry-on suitcases.
A compact section on the right side of the garage houses an additional electrical system – yes, you read that right. Small Vans Big World fitted a 100 Ah lithium battery, 12V fuses, a DC-DC charger, and a solar charger.
This camper uses the vehicle's stock heating and cooling system, with its controls integrated into the part of the ceiling above the cabin.
Even though you can't enter the van through the passenger-side door, you gain access to other features by sliding that door open. Specifically, a flip-up table you can use outside and a straightforward plumbing system for the sink.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Small Vans Big World The latter comprises two 2.5-gallon (9.5-liter) canisters, one for fresh water and the other for grey water. They can be easily removed and filled or dumped, as needed.
All in all, Small Vans Big World fitted as many luxury items as one can fit in a minivan without making it feel cramped, putting the limited space to excellent use. On top of that, it managed to balance this much-needed practicality with a refined, tasteful design.

Someone Just Paid Nearly $200,000 for a Seven-Year-Old Ford F-150
26 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
This 2019 Ford F-150 has just been sold for an incredible $195,000. While it may sound out of this world for America's most popular truck, there is something special about it. It is an HM Elite Prerunner, which has spent most of its life at the Petersen Automotive Museum.
The 2019 Ford F-150 HM Elite Prerunner is a heavily modified, street-legal off-road machine built by HM Offroad to mimic the capabilities of a Baja Trophy Truck, while retaining the creature comforts that it came with from the factory.
The example that has spent years in the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles, California, has just about 7,700 miles (12,392 kilometers) on the clock. Seven years and 7,700 miles ago, the original owner paid $42,460 to drive it off the showroom floor, which is more than four times less than the price that it has just fetched.
The truck is powered by Ford's 5.0-liter Coyote V8 engine, which produced 395 horsepower (400 metric horsepower) and 400 pound-feet (542 Newton meters) of torque in stock form. But the V8 has been upgraded with an Edelbrock, a new radiator, and MMR timing components, taking output to a whole new level.
Photo: Cars and Bids The transformation also includes a custom 63-gallon fuel cell, dual racing fuel pumps, a Pedal Commander throttle response controller, and an SCT tuning device. However, the listing doesn’t say how much, and the museum doesn't disclose that info, either.
However, similar supercharged 5.0-liter Coyote-based setups typically push these vehicles well past 700 horsepower, so it is probably safe to assume that this truck has been dialed up to produce around that much, but a dyno sheet hasn't been provided to confirm the actual extra oomph that it comes with.
A ten-speed automatic transmission with a SunCoast torque converter puts the power down through the rear wheels. It is, after all, a desert rally truck in the shape of a muscle truck. A custom-fabricated exhaust roars out the drama of the V8 from under the hood.
The 2019 Ford F-150 HM Elite Prerunner wears Agate Black with a red, white, and blue wrap over a black and gray interior. The truck features a race-spec 4130 chromoly roll cage, built to SCORE specifications, which means that the safety structure meets the rigorous rulebook requirements dictated by the premier sanctioning body for desert off-road racing. The roll cage extends fully through the cab, engine bay, and bed.
Photo: Cars and Bids The adventure-ready Ford F-150 also comes with a long-travel setup up front, using KING Shocks 4.0 bypass shocks and bump stops, paired with HM Offroad upper and lower control arms, along with hydraulic swing-set steering.
Out back, it got a fully caged, back-half chassis yielding up to 25 inches of travel, sporting billet 7075 aluminum trailing arms, a custom rear sway bar, and a fabricated 4-inch Trophy Truck rear housing with a 10-inch ring gear and heavy-duty 36-spline axles.
For an intimidating stance, the 2019 Ford F-150 HM Elite Prerunner was fitted with McNeil Racing fiberglass widebody front clips and bedsides, which dramatically widen the track width, making room for the 17-inch Trail-Ready beadlock wheels with a true six-lug trophy truck bolt pattern and massive 40-inch BFGoodrich Mud-Terrain T/A KM3 tires. An R1 Concepts big brake system handles the stopping power.
The vehicle is also equipped with air conditioning because you surely need it while dune-bashing, and with a rear window defroster because you don't know when that might come in handy. Three PRP racing seats in custom Alcantara upholstery, with five-point harnesses, keep the occupants secured. A fire suppression system is on board for those just-in-case moments.
Photo: Cars and Bids The cabin looks like the cockpit of a purebred rally car, hosting a Switch-Pros switch panel, PCI Rae Radios intercom, a Lowrance Elite GPS, a Pioneer touchscreen head unit, and an AutoMeter oil pressure gauge. A custom horn and siren are also on the menu.
Nothing to complain about so far. However, it hasn't been all milk and honey with this truck. It has obviously been forged in the fire. A day out on the sand dunes for a bit of fun ended up with a costly engine replacement.
That was because the person driving it (the listing says it wasn't even an active employee of the museum) did not use the cooling fans installed out back and failed to keep an eye on the gauges. " That person is no longer with the museum, " the seller explains.
The truck was shipped straight to Galpin Ford to assess the engine condition. It was so bad that the truck needed an emergency "heart" transplant. Because of all the systems the vehicle is running, the Check Engine light occasionally comes on, but the Petersen Automotive Museum representative says that is nothing to worry about, because it by no means affects any mechanical or driving condition.
Photo: Cars and Bids This is what the buyer got for $195,000, along with a clean Carfax report, one key, the window sticker, two spare wheels, a spare driveshaft, spare engine oil containers, fire extinguishers, and a jack. Before this purchase on Cars and Bids, the truck had been with the Petersen Museum since 2023.

GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-Screen 1
The GL.iNet Comet Q GL-RMQ1 is a new class of remote KVM devices, and it has something really neat. It is designed to be a single-cable solution. Plug a USB Type-C cable into a device with a Type-C port that supports video, and that is the only cable you need. WiFi handles network connectivity, and the built-in Type-C cable powers the unit, carries the video feed, and sends keyboard, mouse, and remote media to the remote system. One of the neat functions is that, along with being able to control many PCs, you can also connect phones and tablets using this solution.
Here is an Amazon affiliate link to where we bought ours.
GL.iNet Comet Q GL-RMQ1 Hardware Overview
The unit itself has a large 1.8″ touchscreen on its face, but it is like a puck design rather than many of the KVM units that are very boxy. What it is not, however, is small.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-Screen 1
On the rear of the unit, you can see cooling vents, rubber feet, and an integrated USB Type-C cable.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-Bottom 1
That integrated Type-C cable is not huge, but it is nice to grab the unit and have the cable ready. It does, however, mean that if you wanted a Type-A connection, or a Type-A and HDMI, for example, the convenience is not there.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-USB Type-C Connector Cable 1
We plugged it into the Bosgame M5 since that was next to the step, and it is something you can see that is really important here. If you plug it into a system, then it has to boot. If you go from off to on, some systems boot faster than the GL-RMQ1, so that makes it hard to get into the BIOS.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-Screen 2
Once it boots, the little touchscreen is very useful. You can see the IP address, along with the KVM and video connectivity status. You can also set up the unit, for example, by selecting a WiFi SSID and entering a password. Once the initial setup is done, you can then manage it via a browser.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-Screen 3
Something important is that there is another Type-C port. This is a power input, which makes sense since many devices you connect to only have a single Type-C port.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-USB Type-C Port 1
Then there is one more accessory in the box, a little protector that is bright orange. We bought two of these and got the same color. Our guess is that this will eventually get a Sharpie marker on it to help quickly label these with a hostname so we know which is which.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-Rubber Case 1
Here is the protector installed.
GL iNet Remote KVM GL-RMQ1-Rubber Case 2
Next, let us get to using the GL.iNet Comet Q.

source_document.body:
Pivot Energy, an impact-focused independent power producer of distributed-scale solar and energy storage, announced the closing of a $173-million term loan facility for a portfolio of 51 community-scale solar projects totaling 135 MW across six states.
Long-time financial partners First Citizens Bank, Huntington Bank, and BankUnited provided the takeout financing. The facility refinances the projects from Pivot’s construction warehouse and consolidates Pivot’s first three portfolios under a single term structure, marking the company’s first term loan financing. The transaction announced October 8 also frees up capacity in Pivot’s revolving construction facility to support continued construction of additional projects.
“Closing our first term loan across a consolidated portfolio is an important step for Pivot,” said Bret Labadie, CFO at Pivot Energy, which is headquartered in Denver, Colorado. “We’re grateful to First Citizens, Huntington, and BankUnited, who have supported Pivot from the start. This financing gives us the flexibility to grow faster and deliver lasting value where our projects are built, from community investment and agrivoltaics to local jobs and economic development. As the electricity landscape becomes more complex, we’re proud to work alongside utilities, corporate energy buyers, and ratepayers to deliver local, reliable power that strengthens the grid.”
“First Citizens is pleased to continue building on our long-standing relationship with Pivot Energy,” said Mike Lorusso, head of First Citizens Bank’s Energy Finance business. “This financing reflects the strength and diversity of Pivot’s distributed solar portfolio, and we’re proud to support the company through its next stage of growth.”
—This content was contributed by Pivot Energy .

BMW’s New 3 Series Gets a Virtual Visit From the Tuning Fairy
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project
It’s been a couple of weeks since BMW uncovered the new-generation 3 Series , and besides the original stories, and the occasional rendering imagining it in different guises, the premium compact sports sedan hasn’t gotten that much attention from us.
However, the model has just made headlines again, as this one has received a virtual visit from the tuning fairy, as mentioned in the title. But what does that mean exactly? That it is a rendering take on it, because the G50 has yet to hit the assembly line. This means that nobody has one, though you can rest assured that plenty of tuners are already sketching out various aftermarket upgrades for it.
In this case, it wasn’t a tuner that has signed the CGI-infused 2027 BMW 3 Series shown above, but a rendering artist. This car came from @ildar_project on Instagram, shared on social media recently, and the pixel master hasn’t had much to say about it in the caption that accompanies the digital illustrations. But then again, what could have he said? After all, it’s an unofficial tuning take on this model.
Can you tell what’s new just from looking at the pictures and not comparing this rendered machine with the real one? Why, you likely can, because the virtual upgrades are definitely visible. These include a new kidney grille that retains its OEM shape and size, a new hood that is on the extremely vented side of things, and a modified bumper, with new trim on the side vents, a new pattern for the central air intakes, and an apron attached to it.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project The latter has become mandatory for most tuning jobs these days, just like the side skirt attachments, and this rendered new-gen BMW 3 Series also ticks the latter box. The door mirror casings are new, and sport the M colors on them, and out back, we are looking at new bumper trim, a much bigger diffuser with a pair of extra brake lights, and a new ducktail spoiler that is more pronounced compared to the OEM offering.
Just like the skirts on the lower parts of the body, the wheels are also a must when it comes to modern-day tuning jobs. This 3er rides on larger alloys with a Y-spoke design that fill the arches perfectly. But do you know what they do that? Because the car in question sits much closer to the ground, obviously, so the virtual tuning job also included a lowering kit, or perhaps an adjustable air suspension, which would allow the driver to control how many inches the vehicle has between its belly and the road.
To no one’s surprise, the add-ons would be crafted of carbon fiber on a real tuning job for the all-new B MW 3 Series , especially if we are talking about a renowned tuner. Thus, all the extras mentioned above would be made of the lightweight material, and in this case, they provide some contrast against the car’s green finish. The wheels are black, and the daytime running lights are yellow, and these are an OEM feature, in case you forgot.
These will be found on the new BMW M350 xDrive, which basically bridges the gap between the lesser versions of the G50 3 Series and the upcoming M3, which is expected to premiere sometime in 2027 in the (mechanically unrelated) EV guise, and probably in 2028 when it comes to the ICE model.
Photo: Instagram | ildar_project You do remember what powers this model , don’t you? If you said a familiar 3.0-liter straight-six twin-turbocharged engine, then you should pat yourself on the back, because you certainly know your Bimmer powertrains. The assembly features a 48-volt mild-hybrid assistance in this case, and it churns out 437 brake horsepower, which equals 443 metric horsepower and 326 kilowatts. The torque is officially rated at 428 pound-feet (580 Nm), according to the spec sheet.
Everything is channeled to the rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system through a smooth-shifting automatic transmission with eight forward gears. With no outside intervention, the 2027 BMW M350 xDrive Sedan hits 60 mph (97 kph) in just 3.9 seconds. And guess what? That is actually two-tenths of a second faster than the outgoing BMW M3 Sedan in its base guise. The M3 Competition Sedan is one-tenth of a second faster, and the M3 Competition xDrive Sedan hits 60 mph in 3.4 seconds.
Flat-out, the new M350 xDrive does 130 mph (210 kph), and when equipped with sport tires, the top speed is said to increase to 155 mph (250 kph). Pricing for the 2027/2028 model year BMW 3 Series has not yet been announced, but it will in due course, as the first cars are expected to arrive at dealers nationwide probably in the first half of next year.
Before wrapping it up, we have to ask you if you dig the look of this virtually-tuned , new-gen BMW Series. So, do you? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ильдар (@ildar_project)

Over the past few years, LEGO has quietly added an impressive array of plug-powered machines to its block-based lineup, from hybrid racers to battery-powered excavators and garbage trucks. We’ve rounded them up here.
In putting this list together, I thought it best to group the kits by LEGO theme, which also serves as a rough guide to building difficulty. In other words: the further down the page you go, the bigger, badder, and more involved the builds will tend to get – and by the time you get to the app-controlled Caterpillar DX-11 electric drive dozer and Volvo EC500 Hybrid excavator kits, you’ll be looking at some seriously impressive (and seriously expensive) block-based builds.
Along the way, you might also find a number of electric cars, trucks, and equipment options that we’ve covered in these pages. I’ve included links to those posts as well, in order to provide plenty of some real-world context and give you more to explore once you’ve finished building.

1970 Chevy Nova Sat for 40 Years, Now the Owner's Widow Is Selling It With Wrong Engine and Gearbox
15 photos
Photo: Backyard Barn Finds | YouTube
A barn find hunter traveled nearly 16 hours to see the 1970 Chevy Nova SS, figure out if it rolled off the production line with a big-block engine under the hood, and make sure he is taking home the right car, with the right engine and with the right transmission.
Parker Blubaugh of Backyard Barn Finds slides the red door of the garage upward to reveal the 1970 Chevy Nova SS sitting on dollies, with its Tuxedo Black paint covered by a thick layer of dust. He traveled 989 miles (1,592 kilometers) over 15 hours and 36 minutes to see it and maybe trailer it home. He got an email from Christine one day. Two weeks later, he was right there.
Christine's husband, Vladimir, whom everybody called Val, bought the car when he was 18. At the time, he worked as a bagger at the National Grocery Store in Chicago. Christine says he saved every penny and bought the Nova for $3,000. It was his very first new car. Well, not new-new, but the closest thing to new. The downside was that he bought it with no engine.
Nowadays, it has 54,000 miles on the clock, most of them at the drag strip. He used to race at the U.S. 30 Drag Strip, the legendary venue located in Hobart, Indiana, just south of Gary and about 40 miles outside Chicago. It welcomed car enthusiasts starting in 1954 and until its closure in 1984. During that time, it stood at the absolute heart of the golden era of Midwest drag racing.
Photo: Backyard Barn Finds | YouTube He won two competitions there, and Christine has kept his trophies up on a shelf. “It’s very cool,” she says with pride. One of them is from 1970, his very first year with the Chevy Nova. However, she forgot what engine is under the hood.
Val passed away in 2005, she says, but things don’t add up, so she probably meant 2015. He was a policeman for 27 years and retired at the age of 55 on January 15, 2007. If we were to follow stereotypes, drag racing wasn't exactly what policemen would consider as a hobby. He also tried his own business as an equipment manufacturer. He had two full-time jobs, a wife, and two children.
In May 2007, the family moved to Yellville, Arkansas. They wanted to live in the mountains and in the woods. They had had enough of Chicago. Yellville seemed like a paradise to the people fed up with the concrete jungle.
Photo: Backyard Barn Finds | YouTube Parker wants to buy the 1970 Chevy Nova SS. Back in 1970, the model hit the market with a starting price of $2,978. Nowadays, while the Nova SS 350 small-block cars sell for anything between $25,000 and $45,000 nowadays, the big-block Nova SS 396s go well beyond the $100,000 mark if they are well-maintained, restored examples.
Parker wants to make a fair offer, but it isn’t easy considering that they don’t know what engine sits under the hood. The car did roll off the production line with the 396, but the one who sold it to him had blown the original engine.
